chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not perform Sajdah upon gold, nor upon silver.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform Sajdah on gold or silver surfaces?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a legal ruling on the validity of Sajdah, prohibiting prostration on surfaces of gold or silver to distinguish between humble worship and ostentatious display. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as a recommendation against using precious metals for prayer mats or floors, reflecting the principle of avoiding extravagance in acts of devotion. The ruling underscores the spiritual purity required in prayer by ensuring the physical act remains grounded in simplicity rather than material wealth.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Neither perform Sajdah upon the gold, nor the silver’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus from Ya’qub who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must not perform Sajdah (prostration) on gold or on silver.’”
